item.title: Two women's college basketball teams score on their own baskets in the same day
item.description: New Mexico State and Northwestern State each scored on their own basket on the same day, delivering two of college basketball's most embarrassing moments.
item.content:encoded:
Apparently, knowing which basket you’re supposed to score on is no longer a prerequisite for playing college basketball. Of course, I’m joking, but if you saw the lowlights from the New Mexico State and Northwestern State women’s basketball teams, you might not be so sure. Each team delivered a spectacularly embarrassing moment Friday by gifting the opposing team points while scoring on the wrong basket.

Yes, you read that correctly. Twice. On the same day in college basketball, two different women’s teams scored on their own baskets.

The first disaster came during Northwestern State’s matchup against Arkansas, when Lady Demons guard Karma Wynn inexplicably put the ball into the Razorbacks’ basket on an inbounds play in the backcourt. This was after an offensive foul, too. They were guarding the basket, got a stop, and Wynn still brain-farted and gave Arkansas free points.

ROYALS IMPLODE WITH 3 ERRORS AS METS' CARSON BENGE SCORES LITTLE LEAGUE HOME RUN TO OPEN GAME VS KC

The reaction from the Northwestern State bench said just about everything you need to know. An assistant coach buried her head into her clipboard, while teammates just about leaped out of their seats in shock. Arkansas was handed two free points, and the Razorbacks went on to win big, 89-59.

But just when you thought we'd reached peak basketball stupidity, New Mexico State decided to raise the bar. This one has an interesting twist, so stay in your seat.

With just over 20 seconds remaining against Southern Utah, New Mexico State trailed 61-60. Guard Emma Christiana made a great play by stealing an inbounds pass, then kept going toward the wrong end of the court. She effortlessly laid the ball into her own basket, but judging by her initial reaction and those of the people in the stands, they had no idea Southern Utah had taken the lead in the most insane way.

With the game on the line, Christiana scored two points for the other team. Even crazier: The scorekeeper didn't notice the blunder either. On the broadcast, you would've thought, by the scoreboard, that New Mexico State took the lead.

WNBA FAN GOES VIRAL FOR HALF-COURT SHOT HORROR SHOW THAT LEFT HIM SPRAWLED ON THE COURT

Apparently, even the person responsible for keeping score couldn't comprehend that someone had just scored on the wrong basket. At that point, you almost have to wonder whether anyone in the building knew what was happening. What a mess.

And somehow, despite literally helping Southern Utah take a 63-60 lead, New Mexico State pulled off the win. Freshman Stacy Chovino scored twice in the final seconds, including the game-winning basket with two seconds remaining, on the correct basket, to give the Aggies a stunning 64-63 victory.

Imagine winning a basketball game after scoring for your opponent in the final 30 seconds. That's almost more impressive than the mistake itself.

Two teams. Two own baskets. One afternoon.

Somewhere, a youth basketball coach is preparing a very important PowerPoint presentation titled, "Which Basket Is Ours?" Because apparently, we need to go back to basics.

item.title: White House trashes 'peanut-sized brain' Jimmy Kimmel after host demands Trump 'resign'
item.description: The White House fired back at Jimmy Kimmel after the ABC late-night host called on President Donald Trump to resign, with spokesman Davis Ingle saying his brain has "rotted."
item.content:encoded:
The White House took aim at late-night host Jimmy Kimmel Friday, declaring that his brain has "rotted" after the comedian called on President Donald Trump to "resign."

"Jimmy Kimmel’s case of Trump Derangement Syndrome is so advanced that it has completely rotted his peanut-sized brain," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital.

"He’s far more entertaining when you’re laughing at him than with him, but unfortunately, his real talent is his failing ratings," Ingle added. "This statement took more brain cells to write than the average Jimmy Kimmel joke."

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

The response followed a string of Trump-focused monologues from Kimmel after the midterm elections, with the ABC host celebrating what he described as a Democratic "blue wave" on Tuesday.

During his Wednesday night monologue, Kimmel called on Trump to resign and rejected the president's claim that Republicans would have fared better had he been on the ballot.

"That is such crap," Kimmel said. "You were on the ballot. You’re like dog hair. You’re on everything. You’ve infected every nook and cranny of our lives. You divided this country like no one ever divided it before. The only time you ever brought us together was yesterday, when we all teamed up to get rid of you!"

Kimmel also referred to the president as "Nappy Gilmore" while showing an imagine of Trump appearing to be asleep during a White House meeting, before urging him to "resign."

"Quit already, just quit. Nobody wants you. Even you don’t want to be president anymore. Take that billion dollars’ worth of crypto, buy an island. Maybe Epstein’s island? Wouldn’t that be a perfect end to this story!" Kimmel added.

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

Later in the broadcast, Kimmel addressed a statement Ingle provided to Fox News Digital earlier in the week following the election, in which the spokesman labeled the host a "no-talent loser who has beclowned himself with tanking ratings."

That earlier White House statement had added that Kimmel is "so devoid of actual talent that nobody with any commonsense would ever watch him unless it was to laugh at him."

"Which is kind of the point of the show, but apparently I’ve beclowned myself once again," Kimmel said, acknowledging the statement on his show and referring to Ingle as "Danny Dingle." 

"The last thing I want to do is tell you how to do your job, Danny Dingle, but today seems like a bad day for you to call me a loser," the host added. 

WHITE HOUSE LAUGHS OFF 'BECLOWNED' JIMMY KIMMEL AFTER CRUDE PERSONAL JABS AT NEW PRESS SECRETARY

Responding to Kimmel’s post-election coverage earlier in the week, media commentator and Hollywood in Toto editor Christian Toto suggested the host's relationship with ABC could face growing financial pressure.

"Jimmy Kimmel long ago traded in comedy for activism. He's a DNC apparatchik, pushing party talking points and occasionally cracking wise along the way. This week's response to the midterms is nothing new," Toto told Fox News Digital Wednesday.

"What is new, though, is the tightrope he's walking with ABC. The network wants sizable budget cuts to keep the show afloat. The two sides will likely come up with a compromise, because, for ABC suits, the show's propaganda purposes overshadow financial concerns. But for how long?" Toto added.

SETH MEYERS, JOHN OLIVER TELL JIMMY KIMMEL HE'S THEIR 'BULLETPROOF VEST' WHEN IT COMES TO TRUMP

Fox News Digital’s Hanna Panreck contributed to this report.

item.title: Browns to start Shedeur Sanders at quarterback as Deshaun Watson remains in concussion protocol
item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season against the New Orleans Saints after Deshaun Watson entered the concussion protocol.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time this season, Shedeur Sanders will be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns.

Deshaun Watson has been in the concussion protocol all week and has not practiced, so Browns coach Todd Monken said Sanders will start. Monken praised Sanders’ performance in practice.

"I liked his confidence and the way he operated. He looked very comfortable in terms of getting our guys in and out of the huddle and I thought he threw the ball extremely well," Monken said of Sanders.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Watson could clear the concussion protocol on Saturday, but after missing three days of practice, the Browns will start Sanders regardless of whether Watson is cleared. Sanders entered the game for four plays last week when Watson left to undergo a concussion evaluation, completing two passes for 2 yards.

Watson returned to the game after being cleared by an unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant. The 10-year veteran began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night, when he was placed in the concussion protocol.

The 24-year-old Sanders started the final seven games of his rookie season last year, going 3-4 while completing 56.2% of his passes for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The Browns had a quarterback competition throughout training camp, but Watson won the job.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Sanders said his playing time last season was valuable.

"It was valuable, just tapping back into that memory bank, having those reps and everything," Sanders said. "That’s why I’m thankful for this whole offseason and everything and just being out there with the guys each and every day, being able to still get some throws in with them. So I don’t think we lost a step."

The New Orleans Saints, Cleveland’s opponent on Sunday, have struggled defensively, ranking 28th in the league in total defense and 23rd against the pass.

The Browns (5-3) are looking to avoid consecutive losses for the first time this season, while New Orleans (2-5) is coming off its bye week.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: BOBBY BURACK: Ryan Clark claims ESPN interviewed Sophie Cunningham about trans athletes to impress OutKick
item.description: Ryan Clark claims ESPN published a Sophie Cunningham profile about trans athletes in women's sports to impress OutKick after his firing from ESPN.
item.content:encoded:
Former ESPN employee Ryan Clark claims the company published a profile featuring Sophie Cunningham’s comments about trans athletes after his firing to impress OutKick.

ESPN fired Clark more than three months ago, yet he still discusses his ousting on a regular basis. The New York Post summarized his appearance on the "All The Smoke" podcast Thursday.

"Sophie Cunningham says something and they [OutKick] say, ‘A great brand switch for ESPN. Ryan Clark was fired this week and now Sophie Cunningham leads the news,’" Clark said before alleging that ESPN leaked news of his firing to OutKick.

"That’s what they [ESPN] wanted. That’s why you leaked it to [OutKick]. And so I think everything points to it, but I should have, my antenna should have been up more and even with that, there was nothing I could change."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Clark first accused ESPN of coordinating with OutKick to "humiliate" him three days after his firing. However, as we have documented on multiple occasions, that is not accurate.

In short, OutKick learned that Clark was among several employees ESPN planned to lay off as part of its budget cuts. We informed the network that we were going to report the news because Clark was the most notable name on the list. (We also reported Cam Newton’s ousting when we learned of that news the next day).

Amid an email exchange with ESPN PR about our reporting, an executive informed Clark during a commercial break on "NFL Live" that he would be laid off. He did not return for the next segment.

Our understanding is that the company fired Clark during the show because it feared we would not hold the information until after the broadcast. ESPN management did not want Clark to learn about the decision online.

ESPN did not "humiliate" Clark on purpose. It tried to protect him. The decision, however, backfired — badly. Had ESPN told us that Clark was unaware and asked us to hold the news until he knew, we would have.

Further, ESPN did not leak the news to us. My colleague Dan Zaksheske and I had four independent sources. In fact, ESPN tried to prevent us from breaking it. The fact that ESPN quickly leaked news of Clark’s firing to The Athletic after learning that we had plans to report it suggests that.

That said, Ryan Clark prefers the following narrative: "Those bastards fired me for being too black and leaked the news to Bobby Burack and OutKick."

He believes that version of the story will drum up more sympathy for him. Maybe it will.

To be clear, Clark actually claimed that he "couldn’t be too black" during his time at the network. We are only being partly sarcastic.

Now, let’s address his reference to the Sophie Cunningham profile. The profile generated headlines and protests outside WNBA games because Cunningham voiced support for keeping trans athletes out of girls’ sports.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men," Cunningham told ESPN.

Damn her for extending love while wanting to keep little girls safe!

Clark claimed ESPN profiled Cunningham to show OutKick that it had completed a "brand switch."

Not quite.

For one, the profile was conducted in February. The story was held until July to line up with the WNBA season.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Finally, it is time for Ryan Clark to move on.

ESPN fired him more than three months ago. He has continued to blame everyone but himself for the decision. He has blamed his former bosses, OutKick, Clay Travis, Dan Zaksheske, me and the "culture change."

In reality, none of us are to blame.

Ryan Clark is to blame. He got himself fired.

ESPN fired him because he was toxic. He made false statements about the role Louisiana police allegedly played in the death of former LSU Tigers wide receiver Kyren Lacy. He shamed Robert Griffin III for marrying a white woman. He race-baited by trade. He undermined and disrespected Peter Schrager on air. He shouted the F-word at Schrager off air afterward.

Clark was a headache for producers and a migraine for his bosses.

Most notably, Clark did not drive viewership and therefore did not drive revenue. That is not a knock on him. Most sports analysts do not. The difference is that Clark was also a negative stain on the brand.

He was more of a problem than he was worth.

That would be like Pat McAfee failing to produce results despite the perpetual drama surrounding him. Talents such as McAfee, Stephen A. Smith, and Charles Barkley get away with more because their bosses believe they are worth the trouble.

By no metric was Clark worth the trouble he caused.

It is that simple.

That's why he was fired.

All the claims about racism, OutKick and coordinated leaks are a cope. Clark is too weak to acknowledge the obvious: He was not good enough to be that toxic.

item.title: Craig Carton rips Chiefs teammates for not helping embattled Rashee Rice avoid bankruptcy
item.description: Rashee Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy with $3.45 million in debts, and Craig Carton is asking why his Chiefs teammates haven't stepped up.
item.content:encoded:
It was revealed this week that Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, with the embattled star reporting $3.45 million in debts.

OutKick's Craig Carton discussed the news on the Friday edition of "The Craig Carton Show," and presented an angle you're probably not going to hear anywhere else.

"He's still on that rookie contract, right?" Carton began. "Four years, about $6.5 million, and it's all gone, and now he had to make the humbling decision to publicly file for bankruptcy. That sucks having to do that. I get no joy out of that — I actually feel bad for Rashee Rice."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I'm not one of these guys that gloats and likes watching the downfall of athletes financially, but it pisses me off because he is surrounded by multi-millionaires," he continued. "Guys that we keep getting told are like family to him. That are brothers to him. That cared so much about him two years ago when he had that ludicrous car accident."

He pointed out how numerous Chiefs wore "Free No. 4" shirts when Rice was facing both criminal charges and civil lawsuits, some of which are still pending.

CRAIG REACTS TO RASHEE RICE FILING FOR CHAPTER 7 BANKRUPTCY, CALLS OUT HIS TEAMMATES&THE CHIEFS ORGANIZATION - LISTEN NOW

But he wondered where that same support was from a team said to have a strong relationship in the locker room.

"That's solidarity with a teammate and the public be damned; 'We know he did something wrong, but we have his back.' Well, where are you today?" he asked. "Now, I want to be very clear about this: it's not their responsibility to bail him out financially. I'm not saying it is, but it's what a friend would do.

"It's what a brother would do if you had the available funds yourself to help him out."

item.title: Secret Service arrests armed Venezuelan migrant near White House over alleged Trump assassination threat
item.description: Secret Service officers arrested a Venezuelan migrant in Washington, D.C., after finding guns in a stolen vehicle and hearing an alleged threat against President Donald Trump.
item.content:encoded:
An illegal immigrant from Venezuela was arrested near the White House on Thursday after he was allegedly found inside a stolen vehicle carrying multiple guns and reportedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

U.S. Secret Service officers approached the suspect Thursday evening after spotting him "acting suspicious in his car while it was parked on Constitution Avenue in Washington, D.C.," DHS told Fox News.

The suspect told officers that he heard voices in his head telling him to come to the nation's capital and kill Trump, DHS said.

Officers subsequently learned that the vehicle had been reported stolen, and the suspect admitted to having weapons inside, according to DHS.

CAR RAMS INTO WHITE HOUSE BARRICADE, SUSPECT ARRESTED: OFFICIALS

A search of the vehicle reportedly turned up three firearms, including an AR-15-style rifle and two handguns, along with dozens of rounds of ammunition.

The suspect was identified as Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, who illegally entered the country through Texas in March 2024 and was subsequently arrested by U.S. Border Patrol, according to officials. 

He was later released into the country under the Biden administration, authorities said. 

Following his arrest, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer for Chrinos with the U.S. Marshals Service, where he is currently in custody.

The U.S. Secret Service said the incident reflects a growing threat posed by armed individuals "drawn to the White House complex."

"This is the latest example of Secret Service personnel relying on extensive training and experience to deescalate a volatile situation that posed an imminent threat to our protectees and other Americans," U.S. Secret Service Director Sean Curran said in a statement.

"While our personnel are trained to respond to situations like this and we remain confident in our tactics, we are alarmed by the increase in threat cases that continue to arise."

In order to disrupt threats before they arrive in Washington, Curran said the agency will continue to "focus on proactively investigating and identifying individuals" who raise suspicion.

SECRET SERVICE DETAINS, QUESTIONS INDIVIDUAL WHO DROVE VEHICLE INTO BARRICADE NEAR WHITE HOUSE

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin also commended the Secret Service for intervening before the suspect could harm anyone.

"This is just an example of the incredible work done by the men and women of the Secret Service every single day as they put their lives on the line to protect our nation’s leaders," Mullin said in a statement. 

Chrinos has been charged with carrying a rifle outside of a home or business, three counts of unlawful transportation of a firearm, three counts of possessing an unregistered firearm, three counts of possessing unregistered ammunition, possession of certain dangerous weapons, carrying a pistol without a license, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, theft and receiving stolen property.

The latest incident comes amid a series of alarming encounters and security breaches near the nation's capital.

Just three months ago, a California resident was found near Capitol Hill after driving cross-country with an operational 10-foot guillotine in his pickup truck. He was identified as Philan-Tam-Duy Le.

In two separate but similar incidents, suspects also rammed vehicles into security barricades near the White House in March 2026 and October 2025.

item.title: World's tallest women's college basketball player makes her debut for Texas Tech
item.description: Stephanie Okechukwu posted 10 rebounds and three blocks in her Texas Tech debut, and the NCAA just granted the 7-foot-1 Nigerian four years.
item.content:encoded:
It's officially a new era for women's college basketball after Thursday night's debut of 7-foot-1, 21-year-old Nigerian Stephanie Okechukwu at Texas Tech.

Okechukwu, who is classified as a sophomore, had six points, 10 rebounds and three blocks in 21 minutes as Tech won easily 64-37 over Charlotte. The Nigerian tower made her presence felt early in the game when a Charlotte player went up for a simple put-back only to get absolutely stuffed.

Could we be looking at a future Angel Reese stopper? It's early, but fans know they're looking at a force under the basket. "Someone tell her to start doing the finger wag after every block," one fan wrote on Steph's Instagram as a throwback to Dikembe Mutombo's signature move after a block.

ANGEL REESE VS. 7'3" DOUGHY CHINESE TOWER ZHANG ZIYU WAS A BATTLE FOR THE AGES AT THE FIBA WORLD CUP

According to her bio, Okechukwu was born in Nigeria and then somehow ended up playing high school basketball in Japan. In YouTube videos posted earlier this year, the Texas Tech center is seen dominating what looks like high school basketball. In one of the videos, Steph's team wins 119-43.

On Wednesday, Tech announced that the NCAA had granted Okechukwu four years of eligibility. "I think about this every day," Okechukwu said in a social media video.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"It was obviously huge for us," Tech women's basketball coach Krista Gerlich told the media this week. "I feel like the NCAA did a really great thing here because it is for the right reasons. We were expecting two (years of eligibility), we were hoping for three, and to be blessed with four is just out of this world."

Why was there a question about Okechukwu's eligibility? It's unclear. "She hasn't played college basketball," Gerlich promised.

How does a 7-foot-1 Nigerian, by way of Japan, with developed skills just show up in the U.S. out of thin air? That's a great question.

item.title: Kristaps Porzingis stepping away from basketball amid health issues: 'Not where I want to be'
item.description: Kristaps Porzingis cited his ongoing health struggles in his decision to step away, as the Warriors reportedly stopped his $20 million salary payments.
item.content:encoded:
Kristaps Porzingis will not be stepping on the basketball court for the foreseeable future.

The Golden State Warriors big man announced Friday he will "step away" from basketball as he continues to deal with health issues.

"This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn’t respond the way I anticipated. I’m doing good, but I know what it takes and I’m not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself. At this point, I’ve made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love," Porzingis said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense. I’m thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. Onwards and upwards."

ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania has reported that, according to league sources, the franchise has ceased delivering the semimonthly payments he is due on his $20 million salary. The report also indicated that Porzingis is not actively disputing the lack of payments, and the NBA Players' Association has no plans to dispute it.

Porzingis has not taken the floor for the Warriors this season and stepped away from the team the day before the team's training camp began this offseason. The Latvian is reportedly dealing with recurring symptoms tied to Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), which can cause dizziness and fatigue.

Warriors have reportedly stopped paying Kristaps Porzingis' $20 million salary amid mystery illness saga

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Porzingis addressed speculation about his health in an Oct. 14 post on X, and also spoke about online rumors involving "internet doctors" who alleged that he had contracted HIV or AIDS.

"Hello people, I’m working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I’m getting better and better," he wrote on X. "I just have to stay patient, and I believe I’ll be feeling great again soon."

Despite appearing in just 74 total games over the last two seasons battling health issues, the Warriors opted to sign the big man to a two-year, $40 million extension during the offseason. Porzingis has earned more than $253 million in the NBA since making his debut as a New York Knicks in 2015.

OutKick's Mark Harris contributed to this report.

item.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to what happens next on Capitol Hill
item.description: Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan are vying for top House Republican, and incoming progressives challenge Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries for leadership.
item.content:encoded:
The midterms are over. But even more pitched battles are underway.

These are internal House and Senate leadership elections. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., won’t pursue the minority leader post.

President Trump doesn’t always see eye-to-eye with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., but the president hasn’t demanded a change there.

Some incoming House and Senate progressives have expressed their reservations about House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., despite the stunning Democratic wins from Tuesday night.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: A DEMOCRATIC MAJORITY COULD EXPOSE THE LIMITS OF THE PROGRESSIVE AGENDA

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., has long warned he might not support Schumer for Majority Leader.

"If you’re Chuck Schumer, I’m dangerous," El-Sayed advised in late June.

The Michigan Democrat ducked the question when asked about supporting Schumer on NBC just after the election.

"I am going to vote for the option that gives me the best chance of getting money out of politics. Putting money in pockets and passing Medicare for all," said El-Sayed. "I'm interested to see, working with the rest of our caucus, what options we've got."

By Thursday on CNN, El-Sayed was reiterating his support for Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who hasn’t announced he’s running for anything.

"I think he'd be an amazing Senate majority leader," said El-Sayed of Van Hollen.

But even other newcomers weren’t committing to Schumer.

"No, I will not (support Schumer)," Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton, D-Kan., said on Fox before the election. "And I've already said I'm not going to vote (for him)."

"I think it's really clear that both parties are ready for a new generation of leadership," Sen.-elect Annie Andrews, D-S.C., told colleague Bret Baier.

"I told Sen. Schumer that I'm going to support somebody else," offered Sen.-elect Troy Jackson, D-Maine.

But Schumer is shrugging that off.

"I'll be re-elected as majority leader," Schumer said when asked by reporters on Wednesday. "But the issue is focusing on the American people and what they want."

Schumer only needs around 29 of his members to support him in a secret caucus vote to become majority leader. That’s a majority of expected Senate Democrats who will serve next year.

At least five members of the Democratic Socialists of America are pledging to withhold their support for Jeffries as the first Black House speaker in U.S. history unless they secure commitments for their agenda. The successful candidate for speaker requires an outright majority of the entire House — 218 votes of 435, if all Representatives-elect cast ballots — when the new Congress convenes Jan. 3.

Keep in mind that House Democrats may score more than 260 seats once all races are settled. So, he can afford dozens of defections.

For House Republicans, Johnson may have signaled his future last month when speaking to colleague Aishah Hasnie.

"If God moves on our hearts and says we should go back to my hometown of Shreveport and start a lawn business, I'll do that," said Johnson.

Now it’s far from certain that Johnson will soon channel Groundskeeper Willie from the Simpsons. But perhaps becoming "The Lawnmower Man" is a better option for Johnson than getting mowed down by your own colleagues in a bid for minority leader.

Maybe the grass IS greener back in Louisiana.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., and Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, are running to become the House’s top Republican. House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., wants to return as minority whip. He’s facing a challenge from Rep. August Pfluger, R-Texas.

But here’s the trick. How do these House Republicans win the leadership positions yet maintain their own coalitions? It’s unclear if Republicans think that Jordan and Scalise are right for the party — right now. Both are aligned with President Trump. And some Republicans hope to move past that.

Regardless, Democrats campaigned on two things: the cost of living and holding the Trump administration accountable. But what does the Democrats’ legislative agenda look like? 

This isn’t like 1994, when former House Speaker Newt Gingrich, R-Ga., famously crafted the 10-point Contract with America as a pledge to voters as to what Republicans would do if they flipped the House for the first time in 40 years.

CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER'

Democrats have a host of ideas on what they plan to vote on.

"We have to first get in there and really focus on rolling back the cuts from the one big ugly bill," Sen.-elect Juliana Stratton, D-Ill., promised on CNN.

Also expect votes on renewing expired Obamacare subsidies. Democrats demanded money to offset the costs of rising premiums in exchange for their votes to fund the government. The House finally passed a bill to do that. But the Senate didn’t. The standoff over the Obamacare aid was the key component to last year’s record-breaking, 43-day government shutdown.

"The shutdown sharpened the American people's view of the distinction between the parties on this crucial issue," Schumer said.

Democrats are also focused on a key issue from the midterms: the future of AI and data centers. They’re concerned that AI threatens American jobs.

"This revolt against data centers are just the initial tremors of a bigger AI earthquake that is upending American politics," said Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, chairman of the Progressive Caucus. "And we have to be on the right side of this issue."

There will undoubtedly be votes to end the war in Iran — perhaps by cutting off money for those operations. The House approved three "war powers" resolutions. The Senate green-lighted one. But those machinations did nothing to hem in the president on the war.

Democrats believe that ending the war will reduce gas prices. And that, in turn, will lower the cost of groceries.

Congressional Republicans balked at unwinding tariffs imposed by President Trump. So, there could be votes on that front, too. Democrats believe the election shifted the dynamic of Republicans aligning behind the President in near lockstep.

"This is the time for (Republicans) to show the courage to end this irrational and self-defeating tariff regime that Trump has put in place," said Rep. Greg Stanton, D-Ariz. 

"Most of them realize that the tariffs from a fiscal and economic perspective are completely self-defeating."

However, some Republicans aren’t ready to abandon the old playbook, clinging to the GOP’s hallmark legislative achievement of this Congress.

"I think the tax cuts and the Big, Beautiful Bill were underappreciated by the electorate," Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., proffered.

President Trump signaled he’ll both work with Democrats and deploy his veto pen. But it’s about the math. When all House races are settled, Democrats could control more than 260 House seats. 

That’s astonishing. 

They’re guaranteed 54 Senate seats with Mississippi and Alaska still undecided

It’s about the math. Overriding a veto requires two-thirds of both bodies. That’s 290 in the House and 67 in the Senate. If Democrats hover around 260 seats in the House — and Republicans are ready to ditch the president — hitting the 290 mark isn’t out of reach. 

If Democrats clock in at 56 seats in the Senate, cobbling together 11 GOP votes to reach 67 might be tougher. Especially with GOP Trump antagonists like former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and senators John Cornyn, R-Texas; Bill Cassidy, R-La.; and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., departing. But they’re in range.

It all hinges on what Democrats can pass. And what the president is willing to sign.

item.title: Disrespectful singer who waved Pride flag during the national anthem offers up predictably tone-deaf response
item.description: Jason Brock waved a Pride flag during the national anthem at the Golden State Warriors Pride Night game, and his response to the backlash followed.
item.content:encoded:
The national anthem singer who decided to use our time honoring America by waving a Pride flag before Thursday's Golden State Warriors game has offered up his official response to the backlash ...

Shockingly, it's as tone-deaf as you'd expect.

Weird! Never saw it coming.

EX-NBA PLAYER SAYS LEBRON JAMES SHOULD 'STAND THE F--- STILL' DURING NATIONAL ANTHEM

For those who missed it, the Warriors held their Pride Night for Thursday's home game against Miami. Singer Jason Brock had the honor of performing the pregame national anthem, and promptly whipped out a small Pride flag when he got to the lyrics, "What so proudly we hailed ..." and began waving it around and nodding his head.

The crowd gave a relatively diluted response, and then the cameras panned to several Warriors players who appeared to be laughing.

You would think they were laughing at the absurdity of the situation, which would be a natural response given the disrespect. Nobody knows exactly why they were amused, but Brock was appalled at the notion that it could've been at his disgusting antics.

Take a look:

"Wow I didn’t interpret it like this, but I wasn’t watching the players," he said, via X. "Just because they were laughing doesn’t mean it was because of the anthem."

DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT BEFORE TI’S 10-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER SINGS WNBA FINALS ANTHEM

Amazing. These people are amazing. Regardless of why they were laughing, it's just not the point.

Can't we just sing a normal, respectful national anthem? I don't get it. We just spent weeks breaking down pregame film of the WNBA Finals because nobody wanted to respect our anthem, and now we're waving a Pride flag during it?

What world are we living in? It's not asking a ton. It's really not. We're simply asking you to behave normally during the national anthem. It's quite literally the least you could do in that situation.

Of course, that's just not how the world works in 2026. It's all virtue-signaling and gaslighting. If you're not pandering, you're not trying.

Something as sacred as the Star-Spangled Banner can no longer be done without someone — or some team — hijacking it for some "cause" or some sort of activism.

It's the national anthem. We've done this for hundreds of years. Stand up, pay attention, be respectful and leave the other stuff at home. Do it on your own time.

Not America's.

item.title: Trump's move from Wiles to Miller signals major tactical shift for governing without Congress
item.description: Stephen Miller and Russ Vought have been identifying policies Trump can enact by executive order on immigration, tariffs and government spending.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump tapped Stephen Miller to succeed Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, elevating an adviser who reportedly helped develop plans to advance his agenda without congressional approval as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January.

Miller, Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and White House lawyers have worked since April to identify executive actions Trump could take without new legislation, including measures on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending, Reuters reported Sunday, citing three people familiar with the planning.

TRUMP TOUTS 'ULTIMATE POWER' OF VETO IF DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF HOUSE AND SENATE

In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court handed Trump a significant victory on presidential authority in June, ruling that he had the constitutional power to remove former Federal Trade Commission Commissioner Rebecca Slaughter despite a federal law restricting the president's ability to fire FTC commissioners.

TRUMP REVIVES RARE BUDGET MANEUVER TO RESCIND $810M IN CONGRESSIONALLY APPROVED FUNDS

MIKE JOHNSON'S NO 2 LAUNCHES GOP TAKEOVER BID AS HOUSE FALLS TO DEMOCRATS

TRUMP CONGRATULATES DEMOCRATS AFTER DOMINANT MIDTERMS, SAYS HE LOOKS FORWARD TO WORKING WITH THEM

Another said the Trump administration will continue governing "without Congress, as they've been doing."

STEPHEN MILLER SAYS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION IS PURSUING POLICY TO DEBANK ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

A Trump administration official praised Miller's appointment, particularly given Miller's immigration bona fides.

"A great pick," the official told Fox News Digital. "He has the trust of millions of Americans who understand that reversing mass migration is the crisis of our time."

Miller will begin his new role Monday, and Wiles will move to Trump's political operation.

item.title: Fitness influencer's vacation getaway takes scary turn after headache leads to ICU
item.description: Khiana Smith was rushed by ambulance to a Bali hospital after a severe headache and light sensitivity led to a meningitis diagnosis in the ICU.
item.content:encoded:
A 23-year-old fitness influencer's vacation took a frightening turn after she suddenly became seriously ill in Bali.

Australian fitness coach Khiana Smith said in a TikTok video that she was hospitalized after developing a severe headache and sensitivity to light. She later revealed in another video that she had been diagnosed with meningitis.

Smith said she knew something was wrong when she woke up with what she described as the "worst headache."

DEADLY LEGIONNAIRES' DISEASE OUTBREAK SPARKS CONCERN IN MAJOR US CITY: KNOW THE SYMPTOMS

"I couldn't even get out of bed," Smith said in the TikTok video. "It was so intense I couldn't even open my eyes properly. I was really sensitive to light. I couldn't stand up without falling over."

She initially waited to see whether she would feel better, but said she woke up the following morning feeling "10 times worse." She was eventually taken to a hospital by ambulance, where testing revealed the infection.

Dr. Alfred Joshua, a California-based board-certified emergency room physician and former chief medical officer, told Fox News Digital that Smith's reported symptoms included several warning signs that should be taken seriously.

"She started having symptoms of severe headache, having difficulty with light," Joshua said. "And then she started having difficulty walking, and then eventually slurred speech."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Meningitis occurs when the protective layers surrounding the brain and spinal cord become inflamed, according to Joshua.

Symptoms can include headache, fever, stiff neck and sensitivity to light. Trouble walking or speaking, confusion and extreme tiredness are more serious signs that should prompt immediate medical attention, Joshua said.

The seriousness of the illness can also depend on what is causing it.

Joshua said viral meningitis often resolves on its own, while bacterial meningitis can progress rapidly and requires prompt treatment with antibiotics.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"Certain strains over a couple of hours [can cause] the person [to] get really, really sick," he said.

Doctors initially did not know whether her meningitis was bacterial or viral, according to Smith, so she was being treated for the bacterial form as a precaution.

Smith's condition later appeared to improve enough for her to leave the ICU, but she said she had to return after continuing to experience head pain, light sensitivity and slurred speech. She also reported memory loss, and said swelling in her brain was preventing her from flying home.

When meningitis is suspected, Joshua said doctors can use blood tests, brain imaging and a lumbar puncture to determine whether the infection is bacterial, viral or caused by something else.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Smith's experience has highlighted a concern for travelers who become seriously ill far from home.

Joshua said recommended vaccines can protect against some forms of bacterial meningitis, and advised travelers to consider insurance that includes medical evacuation coverage.

Smith's mother also stressed the importance of travel insurance, saying her daughter's hospital expenses were covered because she had purchased a policy before leaving Australia.

Joshua said worsening symptoms, including changes in speech, walking or other brain functions, should not be ignored.

"When symptoms are progressing in a more complicated manner with neurological dysfunction, do not wait and try to see this out," he said. "Go and seek prompt emergency treatment."

Fox News Digital reached out to Smith for comment.

Darnold, who will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals because of a quad injury, also suffered a cracked rib on the second play of Monday night’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Lock said he knew right away Darnold was hurt despite the starter not saying anything.

item.title: Houston mayor bolts early from ICE cooperation after blue wave crashes in Texas
item.description: Houston Mayor John Whitmire bars police from notifying ICE during nonviolent stops despite defeated Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott's order.
item.content:encoded:
The Democratic mayor of America's fourth-largest city is reversing course on cooperation with federal immigration authorities despite an executive order from defeated Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott that threatened the loss of millions in state funding for noncompliance.

The Lone Star State swung blue for the first time since its new senator-elect, James Talarico, was born, and Houston Mayor John Whitmire wasted no time Friday announcing new restrictions on cooperation with ICE.

Whitmire told The New York Times that city police are not permitted to notify ICE if they encounter an illegal immigrant in "nonviolent contacts" like traffic stops or minor offenses.

'WE DIDN'T EXPECT THIS': TEXAS DEMOCRATS STUNNED AS BLUE WAVE TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLD

"If they’re charged with a new crime, we’ll let ICE know as we get them to the jailhouse," he told the paper Friday.

Abbott lost his bid for a fourth term Tuesday, and Talarico flipped one of the state’s Senate seats blue for the first time since Clinton Treasury Secretary Lloyd Bentsen won his final re-election bid in 1988 — seven months before the current senator-elect was born.

Texas’ most recent Democratic governor, Ann Richards, the mother of former longtime Planned Parenthood president Cecile Richards, was elected shortly thereafter in 1990.

Whitmire did not respond to a request for comment but signaled to the Times that he made the decision at least in part because Abbott’s order requiring DHS contact caused "anxiety" among Houstonians.

In a statement put out Friday afternoon, Whitmire said, "I have signed an executive order directing HPD to no longer contact ICE for nonviolent offenses, helping reduce fear in our communities. Thank you to Chief Diaz, our state and local leaders for their collaboration. A step toward building a stronger Houston. Let’s Go to Work."

He also acknowledged Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa won’t take office until January but characterized his decision as "responsible" and "more effective policy."

A DHS spokesperson responded to Whitmire's move in comments to Fox News Digital.

"We remain disappointed that sanctuary politicians seek to limit cooperation with ICE, as our law enforcement are simply fulfilling their sworn duties to serve and protect our communities," the spokesperson said.

"Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country. Seven of the top 10 safest cities in the United States cooperate with ICE. When politicians bar local law enforcement from working with DHS, our law enforcement officers have a more visible presence so that we can find and apprehend the criminals let out of jails and back into communities.

The spokesperson pointed to some recent criminal illegal aliens captured by ICE in Houston – including Alexander Montano of Cuba, convicted of willful homicide, burglary and forced entry into a residence.

Vietnamese national Ding Nguyen, also convicted of homicide, along with Guatemalan national Julio Camey, convicted of sex offense against a child, were also mentioned by the spokesperson.

"You write a citation or you warn them, and they go about their way. No contact with [ICE] over nonviolent, non-jailable offenses," Whitmire told the AP.

A previous policy enacted in March by Whitmire and Police Chief Noe Diaz stipulated that if a background check revealed an immigration-related warrant, a sergeant would be called to oversee ICE involvement, according to Houston’s FOX affiliate.

The policy also said that if ICE could not make it to the stop within half an hour, the subject would be released.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The Houston City Council subsequently approved an ordinance in April limiting how long officers could detain individuals while awaiting ICE agents, but Whitmire backed revisions after Abbott threatened to withhold more than $100 million in state funding and then-Attorney General Ken Paxton launched an investigation into the city's immigration policies.

The revised policy restored greater discretion for officers to contact ICE and wait for federal agents during encounters involving civil immigration warrants. Whitmire's latest announcement would instead limit such notifications to encounters involving jailable offenses, marking a return to the restrictions city lawmakers initially sought.

item.title: ESPN's Matt Barrie is a man of the people, tells audience to 'unfriend' anyone with a wedding this weekend
item.description: ESPN's Matt Barrie delivered an impassioned plea during the UTSA and FAU game, urging college football fans to skip all fall weddings this Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
I've said it numerous times before, but college football is practically a religion to the fans who consume it every weekend.

Saturdays during the fall are seen as sacred days where people put their differences aside and come together to cheer for their team.

By that logic, anyone who tries to disrupt a college football fan's Saturday should be seen as someone whose views are incongruent with the hardcore fan's, even if their intentions are pure.

A LIST OF THE BEST COLLEGE GAMEDAY SIGNS AT LSU DURING SHOW'S 500TH EPISODE

All that is to say, the war being waged between college football fanatics and fall weddings is one that isn't slowing down anytime soon.

I've gone on record as saying that if you choose to get married on a college football Saturday, you can expect a gift on your registry from me and an empty seat, because I ain't going.

JOSH PATE DISCUSSES NEW ESPN SHOW, FOUR FACES OF ESPN, PAT MCAFEE AND FUTURE OF MEDIA COMPANY WITH OUTKICK

Some may call this childish or accuse me of putting my hobbies before my friends and family, but I'm not alone.

There are millions of other psychos in this country who have also adopted this stance, and one of them is none other than ESPN's Matt Barrie.

Barrie is known for his college football coverage for The Worldwide Leader, and during Thursday night's game between UTSA and FAU, the longtime CFB host decided to lobby against fall weddings with an impassioned plea to all the other fellow psychos.

"I need to say something, and I've never been more serious about something in college football," Barrie said while looking at a juicy weekend slate full of ranked-on-ranked matchups. "If you've got anyone getting married this Saturday, unfamily them or unfriend them, and don't go."

One. Of. Us.

Matt Barrie is alright in my book, because although this will get him skewered by all the uptight casuals, he understands his true audience.

PAT MCAFEE HAS OFFICIALLY SURPASSED STEPHEN A SMITH AS THE FACE OF ESPN

Anyone who was intently watching UTSA and FAU duke it out on a Thursday evening is someone who resonates with every word Barrie uttered.

As a matter of fact, I think it's safe to say Barrie was preaching to the choir.

If you're watching an AAC game on Thursday instead of doing literally anything else, there isn't a snowball's chance in hell you're going to a wedding this Saturday.

Not to worry, Matt! There will be no need to "unfriend" or "unfamily" this weekend.

We're in this "no fall weddings" thing together.

item.title: One popular fruit may support brain and heart health as you age, experts say
item.description: Harvard researcher Walter Willett eats blueberries almost daily for heart and brain health. Here's what studies say about the polyphenol-rich fruit.
item.content:encoded:
A cup of blueberries can give your breakfast a boost and experts say it may also support heart and brain health.

Walter Willett, an 81-year-old Harvard nutrition researcher known for decades of work on diet and chronic disease, recently told The Washington Post that he eats blueberries almost every day, usually adding them to oatmeal with Greek yogurt and nuts.

"In study after study, berries appear to be protective against neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease," Willett told the outlet. "It's an area where we need more research, but berries do seem to stand out, especially blueberries."

NATURAL COMPOUND IN BLUEBERRIES AND GRAPES MAY UNLOCK FAT-BURNING PROCESS IN MUSCLE CELLS

The fruit is one of the most researched, along with apples, bananas and citrus fruits, according to experts, and studies have long examined blueberries' effects on blood vessels and cognition.

In a six-month study of 115 adults with metabolic syndrome, participants who consumed the equivalent of about a cup of blueberries daily showed improvements in blood-vessel function and arterial stiffness, Dr. Nadim Geloo, Virginia-based senior medical director of Abbott's structural heart division, told Fox News Digital.

POPULAR FOOD COULD BOOST HEART HEALTH, BUT THE AMOUNT YOU NEED TO EAT MAY SURPRISE YOU

That doesn't mean they directly prevent heart attacks or strokes, however. 

"Most [studies] small and short, often use freeze-dried powder rather than whole fruit, measure markers like blood vessel function rather than actual heart attacks or strokes and are frequently funded by the blueberry industry," Geloo said.

Some studies have also found improvements in memory and other cognitive measures, especially among older adults, though Dr. Michael Aziz, an internist and physician at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City, noted that those effects were modest and research has not shown blueberries can prevent Alzheimer's disease.

COMMON KITCHEN STAPLE MAY SHARPEN YOUR BRAIN, AND IT ONLY TAKES 2 TABLESPOONS

California-based biomedical researcher Rhonda Patrick also recently spoke about blueberries' benefits for heart and brain health on her FoundMyFitness podcast. 

"The strongest benefit is vascular," she said.

Patrick called blueberries "one of the better-supported polyphenol-rich foods," referring to their antioxidant properties, and also said a "practical dose" is about a cup a day.

THE 8 HEALTHIEST BEANS YOU SHOULD BE EATING MORE OFTEN, ACCORDING TO NUTRITION EXPERT

She noted that studies in older adults have also found improvements in some measures of memory and cognitive flexibility.

Longer-term observational studies have also linked berry intake with slower cognitive decline, but they cannot prove blueberries caused the difference.

Nonetheless, experts say it's still worth eating them.

"While there is no 'magic bullet,' there's nothing to lose by including more berries in your diet," Elisa Bremner, a New York-based registered dietitian nutritionist, told Fox News Digital. 

She, too, eats them nearly every day, Bremner said. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I have heard blueberries called 'brainberries,' due to all the research on cognitive function associated with them," she said.

One cup of blueberries also provides about 3.6 grams of fiber, Bremner noted, which helps slow digestion, and pairing blueberries with protein-rich foods such as yogurt may further slow the release of sugar.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Fresh and frozen blueberries are both practical options, Bremner said, noting that frozen fruit can be a convenient, lower-cost way to eat fruit year-round.

Since the evidence does not show that everyone needs to eat exactly a cup daily or that blueberries can prevent disease, Bremner recommends eating a varied, balanced diet rather than relying on one fruit.

Willett also told The Washington Post that his overall approach emphasizes whole grains, fruits and vegetables, plant-based proteins, healthy fats and modest amounts of meat and dairy.

item.title: Russell Brand police interrogation video emerges as new rape investigations loom after conviction
item.description: Russell Brand told police he kissed "hundreds" and called rape claims "fictitious" in newly released interview footage before his guilty verdict.
item.content:encoded:
Russell Brand insisted he had never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity as he faced rape and sexual assault allegations that would ultimately lead to his conviction.

Newly released police video obtained by Fox News Digital shows Brand defending his sexual history during questioning by London's Metropolitan Police.

In a December 2023 interview, Brand, now 51, sat alongside his attorney and delivered a lengthy prepared statement to detectives, maintaining that his encounters were consensual.

RUSSELL BRAND FOUND GUILTY OF ONE COUNT OF RAPE AND THREE COUNTS OF SEXUAL ASSAULT

"As I’ve repeatedly stated publicly … I led a very promiscuous life in the past, which I’ve spent years openly denouncing. I’ve never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity," Brand said.

He then criticized the September 2023 investigation by several media outlets, which first brought numerous allegations against him into the public spotlight.

Brand described the reporting as "defamatory and fictitious," suggesting encounters that had been consensual were later "invented or reimagined" as misconduct.

WATCH: RUSSELL BRAND POLICE INTERVIEW FOOTAGE RELEASED AFTER RAPE CONVICTION

"At present, I don’t recall the names of the complainants or meeting them," he told investigators. "However, it’s entirely possible that I may have encountered them, and we may have engaged in consensual sexual activity, or physical contact."

Brand also described kissing hundreds of members of the public during press events, book signings and other public appearances.

"I did my best to be accessible and non-discriminatory and loving," he said. "I spent a lot of time at these events."

The actor acknowledged making provocative jokes and comments to people and occasionally asking casual sexual partners to leave shortly after an encounter.

RUSSELL BRAND ACCUSED OF RAPE, SEXUAL ABUSE OF 4 WOMEN; COMEDIAN DENIES ‘SERIOUS CRIMINAL ALLEGATIONS’

But when detectives pressed him about specific allegations, Brand largely declined to elaborate, repeatedly telling officers he had "nothing further to add."

"I do not intend to respond to your questions without sufficient time to consider the information to answer accurately," he said.

The video was released Thursday, Nov. 5, following a jury's decision to find Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

The actor denied the charges throughout the proceedings.

The comedian was taken into custody following the verdict and is due to be sentenced Monday, Nov. 9, at London's Southwark Crown Court, according to the Metropolitan Police.

Brand's legal troubles could extend beyond his four convictions.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed to Fox News Digital that detectives are continuing to investigate rape allegations made by two additional women.

"The Met's investigation into allegations of rape made by two women remains ongoing," a spokesperson said. "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations."

The spokesperson added that case files had been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service and that detectives remained in contact with prosecutors as further investigative work continued.

Brand faced three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009 during his trial.

During the trial, Brand acknowledged being "reckless" and using his fame to pursue sexual relationships but maintained that the encounters were consensual. He told jurors that consent was "fundamental, essential and necessary."

Brand denied forcing any of the women to engage in sexual activity against their will.

The prospect of prison was already hanging over Brand weeks before the jury delivered its verdict.

During an Oct. 11 episode of "Sunday Service with The Brands," his wife, Laura Gallacher, read a message from a supporter who had spent five years in prison and offered the comedian words of encouragement.

"You will get through it … The presence of God is everywhere — in prison as well," one supporter wrote.

Brand immediately interrupted.

"I don’t like things where it’s like, you might have to go to prison," he told Laura.

"No, I know," she responded, acknowledging that incarceration was a possible outcome of the trial.

"That's the nature of what a trial is," Laura said.

Brand conceded that possibility.

"That’s one of the challenges," he replied.

The couple ended the episode by praying to God "for peace and love and for all the participants in this trial or any trial."

item.title: Florida dad makes final FaceTime call to wife before dying in flash flood
item.description: Joshua Bennett's wife described a frantic FaceTime call from her husband as floodwaters trapped his truck on a Brevard County road before the line went dead.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida father died after his vehicle became trapped in flash floodwaters, with his wife now sharing the details of a desperate final call before his death.

Joshua Bennett, 34, of Palm Bay, died Monday after heavy rainfall triggered flooding in Brevard County, along Florida's east-central coast.

Bennett had reportedly left home to buy coffee when he encountered the rising floodwaters, according to WESH 2 News.

MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED

His wife, Stacy Petit Bennett, told the outlet her husband called her in a panic as his truck became surrounded by floodwaters on San Filippo Drive.

"He called me on FaceTime, and he was just crying, like, 'I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do,'" Stacy Petit Bennett said.

"And he said he's in the middle of a river, and his car is, like, submerged with water all around."

Stacy Petit Bennett urged her husband to break a window before the call abruptly disconnected. She said she called 911 and spent hours trying to get help for her husband.

NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING'

Bennett's widow described him as an "amazing husband and dad."

"Every life is important, and everyone deserves a chance to be rescued. To be saved. He was just 34 years old. His kids are young," she said, according to WESH 2 News.

Bennett was a father of four, including three children with special needs, according to his wife. 

His children include twin daughters who were born prematurely.

His wife said their children have been asking when their father would be coming home.

"He's not here. I don't have my support system. They don't have their father," Stacy Petit Bennett said.

Bennett was one of two people who died during the flooding in Brevard County. 

The other victim, Archie Richards, 78, was found dead inside his vehicle near Richards Lane and Hall Road, according to WESH 2 News, citing the Brevard County Sheriff's Office.

Fox News Digital reached out to Brevard County officials for more information.

Other deadly flooding incidents have claimed lives in recent months.

In October, a 24-year-old French travel influencer was among three women killed in Nicaragua when a pickup truck carrying travelers was swept away by strong currents.

Earlier this summer, a Utah family of five died after flash floodwaters swept through a hiking and canyoneering area near Sunglow Campground in Fishlake National Forest.
